scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.finding: A statement's privilege check plans it a second, logical-only time to collect `visitInfo` (`query_visit_info` / `dml_visit_info`, from `Session` in `identity.rs`), where Go's `optimize` checks the `visitInfo` of the one `PlanBuilder` that builds the statement before optimizing it (`CheckPrivilege`)

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: 53 of Go's 86 `ddl.executor` methods (`pkg/ddl/executor.go`) have no counterpart, `DoDDLJob` / `DoDDLJobWrapper` among them: a statement is lowered into this port's own `DdlStatement` (`cluster_ddl.rs` `lower_ddl_with_context`, then a `lower_*` builder) and submitted by `submit_built_job` / `submit_persisted_job_with_retry`; the missing methods include `AlterSchema`, `CreateTableWithInfo` / `BatchCreateTableWithInfo`, `RebaseAutoID`, `ShardRowID`, `ChangeColumn`, `RenameColumn`, `RenameIndex`, `DropView`, `CreatePrimaryKey`, `LockTables`, `CleanupTableLock`, `RepairTable`, `CreateSequence` / `AlterSequence`, the placement-policy, check-constraint, masking-policy, TTL, cache and attribute alters

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: No ingest (fast-reorg) backfill: it falls back to the transactional merge (`tidb-ddl/src/cluster_ddl/add_index.rs`)

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: Cancellation follows Go's `convertJob2RollbackJob` for every action the worker runs; ADD COLUMNAR INDEX has no worker step here, so its `rollingbackAddColumanrIndex` is absent with it

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: A multi-schema change has no `promoteProxyKVDiskFullPause`, whose only producer (`autoPauseAddIndexJobOnKVDiskFull`, the DXF add-index task) Rust lacks (D02, O10)

`foreign_key.rs` enforces a foreign key by reading the referencing rows (`lookup_handles` / `cascade_at_depth`), where Go's `FKCheckExec` checks the referenced keys against the transaction (`checkKeys` / `checkIndexKeys`, with prefetch and locks) and `FKCascadeExec` builds a DELETE/UPDATE sub-statement (`GenCascadeDeleteAST`, `buildFKCascadePlan`) and runs it as an executor; and neither reports `FKCheckRuntimeStats` / `FKCascadeRuntimeStats`

UPDATE and DELETE are driver functions that stream their physical child (`driver/dml.rs` `run_delete_with_physical` / the update runners, `multi_dml.rs`), not Go's `UpdateExec` / `DeleteExec` executors: no executor node owns their `memTracker`, `updatedRowKeys` (`kv.MemAwareHandleMap`, charged per handle) or runtime stats

An Apply whose inner side holds a CTE correlated to the Apply's outer row runs serially (`cte_correlated_to` in `driver/physical_builder.rs`), where Go runs it on the parallel workers: Go's workers share the one CTE producer `buildApply` builds from the original inner plan (`CTEStorageMap`), whose correlated cells no worker binds, so Go answers every such row NULL (gorun: `SELECT a, (WITH c AS (SELECT t2.a FROM t t2 WHERE t2.a <= t.a) SELECT SUM(x.a) FROM c x JOIN c y ON x.a = y.a) FROM t` gives NULL on every row under `tidb_enable_parallel_apply`, 1, 3, 6, ... serially). This port keeps the correct serial answer; an uncorrelated CTE shares its producer across the workers as Go's does
IMPORT INTO refuses (`tidb-session/src/dispatch.rs`)

`ReportMinStartTS` skips sessions waiting on a queued DDL job, but lazy cursor fetch (`execStmtResult.TryDetach`, `tidb_enable_lazy_cursor_fetch`) is not ported, so no session owns a `CursorTracker` (the `tidb-session-cursor` port is unused) and a detached cursor's start TS is not reported; and there is no InfoCache recent-schema TS (`GetAndResetRecentInfoSchemaTS`, InfoSchema V2: I04)

No cross-keyspace runtime (null keyspace only); the next-gen-only surfaces built on it have no port either: the status port's `/dxf/*` and `/ddl/check/*`, and plan replayer's `tidb_cloud_storage_uri` storage (`pkg/planner/extstore` `createGlobalExtStorage`, local files on a classic kernel)

The MPP coordinator lowers a hand-built single-fragment scan DAG and refuses every pushed Selection, TopN and aggregation, where Go builds the fragment/task graph from the physical plan (including disaggregated compute placement)

`pkg/executor/mppcoordmanager` (`MPPCoordinatorManager`: coordinator registration, `detectAndDelete` expiry, the server address) and the RPC server's `ReportMPPTaskStatus` have no port, so TiFlash's task-status reports reach no coordinator; Go's coordinator only asks TiFlash for reports when its plan has a Limit above the table reader (`needReportExecutionSummary`), which the single-fragment scan never builds (M01)

PD's `serviceDiscovery` (`servicediscovery/service_discovery.go`) is not one owner here: member updates and the leader connection live in `pd/cluster.rs` / `pd/retry.rs`, with no per-member `serviceClient`, no `apiCandidateNodes` / `GetServiceClientByKind` (how Go picks a follower for a follower-handled region API) and no `checkServiceModeChanged`
No Cascades memo exploration/implementation in the production optimizer

SQL/PB signature construction and typed vector execution; Go's build-time argument casts (`WrapWithCastAsJSON`, `isnull`'s JSON-to-string cast) are applied per value at evaluation instead of appearing in the expression tree (and EXPLAIN) The planner's `BuiltinFunctionUsageInc` (`expressionRewriter.newFunction`) is not called: it needs the function's `PbCode`, which a planner-built Rust function only gets at pushdown resolution.
No lazy InfoSchema V2, schema-cache-size loader/evictor or InfoCache timestamp ranges

A CLUSTER_* table read is a hand-built fan-out (`ClusterPeerClient::scan_projected`: a TableScan plus at most a DIGEST IN selection, no key ranges, no `Desc`) where Go's planner builds a TableReader whose plan pushed to the `kv.TiDB` stores carries the selections, limit, TopN and aggregation, the key ranges and the scan order; so the receiving handler (`peer_rpc.rs`) builds no `SlowQueryExtractor` for CLUSTER_SLOW_QUERY (Go `PBPlanBuilder.pbToTableScan`'s `Desc` and `buildTimeRangeFromKeyRange`, `predicatePushDown`'s `Extract`, `SetRowLimitHint`), reads every slow-log file forward, and charges no reader tracker; the requesting node reads its own share in-process (`local_cluster_table_rows_for`) instead of through its own coprocessor handler
BRIE statements are classified but never executed

The status port serves `/status`, `/metrics`, `/settings`, `/config`, `/schema`, `/schema_storage`, `/db-table/{tableID}`, `/tables/{colID}/{colTp}/{colFlag}/{colLen}`, `/labels`, `/info`, `/info/all`, `/ddl/history`, `/ddl/owner/resign`, `/txn-gc-states`, `/tiflash/replica`, `/stats/dump/{db}/{table}[/{snapshot}]`, `/plan_replayer/dump/{filename}`, `/optimize_trace/dump/{filename}`, `/stats/priority-queue`, `/test/ttl/trigger/{db}/{table}` and, for a TiKV store, `/regions/meta`, `/regions/hot`, `/regions/{regionID}` and `/tables/{db}/{table}/{regions,ranges,disk-usage,scatter,stop-scatter}` (`region_routes.rs`), `/mvcc/hex/{hexKey}`, `/mvcc/key/{db}/{table}[/{handle}]` (with `decode`), `/mvcc/index/{db}/{table}/{index}[/{handle}]` and `/mvcc/txn/{startTS}/{db}/{table}` (`mvcc_routes.rs`), `/tiflash/replica-deprecated` (`tikv_handler.rs`), `/extract_task/dump` (`extractor_handler.rs` over `tidb-domain` `extract.rs`, Go `ExtractHandle`), and `/upgrade/{start,finish,show}` (`upgrade_handler.rs`) `/debug/gogc`, `/debug/pprof/profile` and `/metrics/profile` (Go `ProfileHandler` over `executor.ProfileBuilder`, `tidb-executor` `inspection_profile.rs`) (`tidb-server/src/http_status.rs`, the profile through `tidb-cpuprofile` over pprof-rs; JSON through Go `WriteData`'s `json.Indent`; the capture-archive download reads `schema_meta.txt` as its writer and `PLAN REPLAYER LOAD` do, where Go's `loadSchemaMeta` misreads it and fails); Go's other routes are absent: `/ingest/*` (Go `ingestctrl`'s rate-limit parameters, which belong to the ingest port, D02), Go's runtime routes `/debug/pprof/{cmdline,symbol,trace}` and the `/debug/pprof/` index (heap, goroutine, ...), `/debug/traceevent`, `/debug/zip`, `/debug/ballast-object-sz`, `/test/ddl/hook` and the `enableTestAPI`-failpoint hooks (`/fail/`, `/test/{mod}/{op}`, `/test/delete/*`); `/dxf/*` and `/ddl/check/*` (next-gen or the system keyspace only, O15) and `/owner_manager/auto_id_service` (starter deploy mode only) are not registered on a classic server
No DXF scheduler/executor managers composed

TopSQL is ported over pprof-rs (`tidb-cpuprofile`, `tidb-topsql-collector`, `tidb-topsql-reporter`, `tidb-topsql`): the status port serves `TopSQLPubSub`, the single-target sink reports to `top-sql.receiver-address`, each command labels its thread `{connID}_{sqlID}`, each statement registers its SQL and plan and labels the thread with both digests, and the profiler's TiDB CPU reaches PROCESSLIST and the statement summary. The DDL worker attaches each job step and each backfill task to the job's SQL (`tidb-ddl` `job_ctx.rs`, Go `ReorgContext.attachTopProfilingInfo`). Unported: the step transaction's request source and resource-group tagger (`prepareTxn`'s `setDDLSourceForDiagnosis` / `getResourceGroupTaggerForTopSQL`), the DXF backfill executor's attach (O10) and the fast-reorg skip checks' (`checkIfTableReorgWorkCanSkip` / `checkIfTempIndexReorgWorkCanSkip`, D02), multi-statement prefetch (`setResourceGroupTaggerForMultiStmtPrefetch`) and executors' `RegisterSQLAndPlanInExecForTopProfiling`; profiler labels follow Go's goroutine inheritance (`labels::inherit`) only into the shuffle, hash-join build, checksum and coprocessor workers, so CPU on other worker threads (index merge, analyze, ...) is attributed to no statement

The DDL scheduler, systable manager, history and MDL readers scan records instead of running SQL on `DdlSessionPool::sess_pool`; the bootstrap stages raw rows; accounts load eagerly where Go loads per active user
